question: In the year of the coronation of Akbar, who among the following was designated as the Wakil of the Mughal kingdom with the title of 'Khan-i-Khanan'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bairam Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1556, the year of Akbar's coronation, Bairam Khan was made the Wakil (regent/chief minister) of the Mughal kingdom and given the title "Khan-i-Khanan" (Khan of Khans). (बैरम खान — खान-ए-खानान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bairam Khan acted as Akbar's guardian and regent during his minority and led the Mughal army to victory in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556) against Hemu.

• His regency ended in 1560 when Akbar took power into his own hands.

NOTE

• Bairam Khan's son was Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, a famous poet (of Hindi "dohas") and one of the Navratnas in Akbar's court.

question: Foods containing fats and carbohydrates are also called ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is energy giving foods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Foods rich in fats and carbohydrates are called "energy-giving foods" because they are the body's main sources of energy. (ऊर्जा देने वाले भोजन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Carbohydrates provide about 4 kcal/gram and fats about 9 kcal/gram of energy.

• Proteins are called body-building foods; vitamins and minerals are protective foods; roughage (dietary fibre) aids digestion.

NOTE

• A balanced diet contains carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, roughage and water in the right proportions.

question: Which of the following is a precious mineral?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Platinum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Platinum" is a precious (noble) metal/mineral, valued like gold and silver for jewellery and industry. (प्लैटिनम — बहुमूल्य धातु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Hematite is an important iron ore; Bauxite is the chief ore of aluminium; Mica is used as an electrical insulator.

• Precious metals include gold, silver and the platinum-group metals.

NOTE

• Platinum is highly resistant to corrosion, has a high melting point, and is used in catalytic converters, jewellery and laboratory equipment.

question: The Betul, Hoshangabad and Chhindwara districts of Madhya Pradesh is a part of which of the following Biosphere Reserves?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pachmarhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve covers the districts of Betul, Hoshangabad (Narmadapuram) and Chhindwara in Madhya Pradesh. (पचमढ़ी बायोस्फीयर रिज़र्व — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve lies in the Satpura Range and includes the Satpura National Park, Bori and Pachmarhi Wildlife Sanctuaries.

• It was designated in 1999 and added to the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) network in 2009.

NOTE

• Manas — Assam; Seshachalam — Andhra Pradesh; Agasthyamalai — Kerala/Tamil Nadu. India has 18 biosphere reserves.

question: Which of the following is the oldest dated forts in India, as first mentioned in Alexander the Great's war records, bringing it to the 4th century BCE?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kangra Fort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kangra Fort (in Himachal Pradesh) is regarded as one of the oldest dated forts in India; it finds mention in the war records of Alexander the Great, dating it to the 4th century BCE. (कांगड़ा किला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Kangra Fort was built by the royal Katoch dynasty and stands at the confluence of the Banganga and Manjhi rivers.

• It is one of the largest forts in the Himalayas and the oldest in India.

NOTE

• Gwalior Fort (MP), Kumbhalgarh Fort (Rajasthan, famous for its long wall) and Mehrangarh Fort (Jodhpur) are also important historical forts.

question: Which of the following is observed on the birthday of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Teachers' Day.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Teachers' Day" is observed in India on 5 September, the birthday of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, a great teacher, philosopher and the second President of India. (शिक्षक दिवस — 5 सितंबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President (1952–1962) and the second President (1962–1967) of India, and received the Bharat Ratna in 1954.

• World Teachers' Day is celebrated on 5 October.

NOTE

• National Engineers' Day — 15 September (birthday of M. Visvesvaraya); Constitution Day — 26 November; National Students' Day relates to Abdul Kalam's birthday (World Students' Day, 15 October).

question: The Kalidas Samman award is presented by which of the following governments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Kalidas Samman" is a prestigious arts award presented by the Government of Madhya Pradesh. It was instituted in 1980. (कालिदास सम्मान — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The award is given annually for excellence in the fields of classical music, classical dance, theatre and the plastic arts (fine arts).

• It is named after the great Sanskrit poet and dramatist Kalidas.

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh also confers the Tansen Samman (Hindustani classical music) and the Maithili Sharan Gupt Samman.

question: In November 2023, who was appointed as the President-elect of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anish Shah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2023, Anish Shah (Managing Director & CEO of Mahindra Group) was appointed as the President-elect of FICCI (Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry). (अनीश शाह — फिक्की)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• FICCI, established in 1927, is the oldest and largest apex business organisation in India; its headquarters is in New Delhi.

• It was founded on the advice of Mahatma Gandhi by G. D. Birla and Purshottamdas Thakurdas.

NOTE

• Other apex industry bodies include CII (Confederation of Indian Industry) and ASSOCHAM (Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India).

question: Which of the following programmes is taken up by the Government of India for improvement of female literacy rates in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (BBBP)" scheme was launched by the Government of India to save and educate the girl child and improve female literacy. (बेटी बचाओ, बेटी पढ़ाओ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The BBBP scheme was launched on 22 January 2015 at Panipat, Haryana, by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

• Its main aims are to prevent female foeticide, improve the child sex ratio (CSR) and promote the education of girls.

NOTE

• It is jointly implemented by the Ministries of Women & Child Development, Health & Family Welfare, and Education.

question: As per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which of the following groups of states is the poorest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021 (released by NITI Aayog), Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand were among the poorest states, with Bihar being the poorest. (बिहार, उत्तर प्रदेश, झारखंड — सबसे ग़रीब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The National MPI is based on the global MPI methodology of the UNDP and OPHI, using three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living across 12 indicators.

• India's first National MPI was released by NITI Aayog in November 2021.

NOTE

• Kerala had the lowest poverty (least multidimensional poverty) among the states in the index.

question: Which folk dance has its roots in Maharashtra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lavani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lavani" is a popular folk dance and song form of Maharashtra, traditionally performed to the beats of the dholki drum. (लावणी — महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lavani is known for its powerful rhythm and has contributed greatly to Marathi folk theatre (Tamasha).

• Garba and Dandiya are folk dances of Gujarat; Bihu is the folk dance of Assam.

NOTE

• Other folk dances: Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Kalbelia (Rajasthan), Chhau (Jharkhand/Odisha/West Bengal).

question: Ravikirti was the court poet of which ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pulakeshin II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ravikirti was the court poet of the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II. He composed the famous Aihole Inscription (Aihole Prashasti) praising the king. (रविकीर्ति — पुलकेशिन द्वितीय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Pulakeshin II (r. c. 610–642 CE) was the greatest ruler of the Chalukya dynasty of Badami (Vatapi); he defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada.

• The Aihole Inscription was written in Sanskrit in the Kannada script.

NOTE

• The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited Pulakeshin II's kingdom. Pulakeshin II also received an embassy from the Persian king Khusrau II.

question: The basic structure of the Indian Constitution stands on the Government of India Act, ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1935.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Much of the basic structure/framework of the Indian Constitution is derived from the Government of India Act, 1935. (भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced provincial autonomy, a proposed All-India Federation, and a bicameral legislature in several provinces.

• Features borrowed from it include the federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary, public service commissions and emergency provisions.

NOTE

• The Act of 1935 was the longest legislation passed by the British Parliament at the time and served as the main blueprint for the Constitution of India.

question: Which of the following is an example of anaerobic activity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jumping.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jumping" is an example of an anaerobic activity — a short, high-intensity exercise done without relying on oxygen for energy. (अवायवीय गतिविधि — कूदना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Anaerobic activities (sprinting, jumping, weight-lifting) are quick and intense, using energy stored in the muscles.

• Aerobic activities (walking, jogging, swimming, cycling) are done over a longer time and use oxygen to produce energy.

NOTE

• During intense anaerobic exercise, muscles may produce lactic acid, which can cause fatigue and cramps.

question: Select the correct order of processes used for water purification in waterworks. 1. Filtration 2. Chlorination 3. Suspended impurity sedimentation 4. Solid impurity sedimentation
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4-3-1-2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sequence of water purification at a waterworks is: 4. Solid impurity sedimentation → 3. Suspended impurity sedimentation → 1. Filtration → 2. Chlorination. (जल शुद्धिकरण का सही क्रम)

◦ First, heavy solid impurities settle, then finer suspended impurities settle, then water is filtered, and finally chlorinated to kill germs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sedimentation allows suspended particles to settle (often aided by alum as a coagulant).

• Filtration passes water through sand/gravel beds; chlorination (disinfection) kills harmful microorganisms.

NOTE

• Chlorination is done last so that treated, filtered water remains free of pathogens until it reaches consumers.

question: Mysore Brothers are known for playing which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Violin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mysore Brothers" (Mysore Nagaraj and Mysore Manjunath) are celebrated violinists of the Carnatic classical tradition. (मैसूर ब्रदर्स — वायलिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• They are known for their duet ("jugalbandi") violin performances and belong to a distinguished family of Carnatic musicians.

• The violin is a bowed string instrument that was adapted into Indian (Carnatic) classical music.

NOTE

• Famous Indian violinists include L. Subramaniam, T. N. Krishnan and N. Rajam; the violin is central to Carnatic music accompaniment.

question: In which of the places was Arya Samaj founded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Arya Samaj" was founded in 1875 at Bombay (Mumbai) by Swami Dayananda Saraswati. (आर्य समाज — बॉम्बे, 1875)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Swami Dayananda gave the slogan "Back to the Vedas" and opposed idol worship, casteism, untouchability and child marriage.

• His famous book is "Satyarth Prakash". The Arya Samaj later established many DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) schools and colleges.

NOTE

• The headquarters of the Arya Samaj were later shifted to Lahore. The organisation played a major role in social and religious reform in North India.

question: 'Waiting for a Visa' is the autobiography of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhimrao Ambedkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Waiting for a Visa" is an autobiographical work by Dr. B. R. (Bhimrao) Ambedkar, describing his personal experiences of untouchability and caste discrimination. (वेटिंग फॉर अ वीज़ा — भीमराव अंबेडकर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution and India's first Law Minister.

• Other works by him include "Annihilation of Caste", "The Problem of the Rupee" and "Who Were the Shudras?".

NOTE

• Dr. Ambedkar was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1990. He is revered as the "Father of the Indian Constitution".

question: What is the standard length of a cricket pitch?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 22 yards.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard length of a cricket pitch (from stump to stump) is 22 yards (about 20.12 metres). (क्रिकेट पिच की मानक लंबाई — 22 गज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The pitch is 10 feet (3.05 m) wide. A chain used in surveying is also 22 yards long — the origin of the pitch length.

• Cricket's laws are maintained by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).

NOTE

• The distance of 22 yards equals 66 feet. There are stumps and bails at each end, 8 feet 8 inches wide.

question: Which of the following groups of ports are located on the bank of the Bay of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haldia and Paradip.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Haldia (West Bengal)" and "Paradip (Odisha)" are major ports located on the eastern coast, on the Bay of Bengal. (हल्दिया और पारादीप — बंगाल की खाड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kandla (Gujarat), Cochin (Kerala) and New Mangalore (Karnataka) are on the western coast (Arabian Sea); Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu) is on the Bay of Bengal.

• Other east-coast ports include Kolkata, Visakhapatnam, Chennai and Ennore.

NOTE

• India has 12 major ports and about 200 minor ports. Visakhapatnam is the deepest landlocked port on the east coast.

question: What is the name of the scheme launched by the Government of India in 2023 to effectively resolve pending contractual disputes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vivad se Vishwas II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vivad se Vishwas II" was launched by the Government of India in 2023 to settle pending contractual disputes of government and government-undertakings. (विवाद से विश्वास II — 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme offers a voluntary settlement mechanism for contractual disputes where an arbitral award or court order is under challenge.

• The earlier "Vivad se Vishwas" scheme (2020) was aimed at resolving direct tax (income tax) disputes.

NOTE

• The scheme was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24 by the Finance Minister to reduce litigation and ease the burden on courts.

question: Shuddhi movement was initiated by which of the following organisations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Shuddhi movement" was initiated by the Arya Samaj (founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati). It aimed at reconverting/purifying people who had converted to other religions and bringing them back into the Hindu fold. (शुद्धि आंदोलन — आर्य समाज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Shuddhi movement was actively promoted by Swami Shraddhanand.

• The Arya Samaj also worked for social reform — against untouchability, casteism and for the education of women.

NOTE

• The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule (1873); the Ramakrishna Mission by Swami Vivekananda (1897).

question: Which financial products are commonly offered by Microfinance Institutions in India?
option_2: Savings, credit and insurance services tailored for low-income individuals
solution_text:
The correct answer is Savings, credit and insurance services tailored for low-income individuals.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) provide small-scale financial services — savings, credit (small loans) and insurance — tailored for low-income individuals and the poor who lack access to formal banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• MFIs promote financial inclusion and often lend through Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), usually without collateral.

• The concept of microfinance was popularised by Muhammad Yunus through the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh (Nobel Peace Prize 2006).

NOTE

• In India, MFIs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI); many operate as NBFC-MFIs.

question: Which edition of the ODI Cricket World Cup was held in India in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC ODI Cricket World Cup 2023, held in India, was the 13th edition of the tournament. (आईसीसी क्रिकेट विश्व कप 2023 — 13वां संस्करण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Australia won the 2023 World Cup, defeating India in the final at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, to claim their 6th title.

• India's Virat Kohli was named Player of the Tournament; Mohammed Shami was the leading wicket-taker.

NOTE

• The first ODI World Cup was held in 1975 in England, won by the West Indies. India won the World Cup in 1983 and 2011.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution has a provision that 'all executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 77 (1).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 77(1) of the Constitution provides that all executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President. (अनुच्छेद 77(1))

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 77 deals with the conduct of business of the Government of India; it also empowers the President to make rules for the transaction and allocation of business (through the Council of Ministers).

• At the state level, the corresponding provision is Article 166 ("in the name of the Governor").

NOTE

• Article 71 — matters relating to the election of the President/Vice-President; Article 75 — appointment of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers; Article 76 — the Attorney-General of India.
